findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed in house dressing to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and dressing was discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.

findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.

findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Observed a bag of chicken to be thawing near pizza oven. Discussed with PIC, education on proper thawing practices was provided, chicken was moved to a pan under running water. Ensure facility is properly thawing TCS items to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a large quantity container holding some ranch dressing with no date marking and a same size container of Caesar dressing with the date 3-30 on it. The Ranch was discarded. Also quantities of pasta salads made in house are observed to have no date marking. Facility is closed Mondays so the pasta salads were fresh yesterday.  Yesterdays date was placed on the items immediately. Take care to properly date mark items and discard items in 7 days. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. 

Make table is holding food at 41F/42F. The internal thermometer reads 37F and the independent thermometer reads 42F.  Service has been called for the unit. Keep lids on dressings at all times and top closed as much as possible. Keep track of food temperatures with a probe thermometer. If the dressings move to 45F or above. Use either time as a control on the dressings or use ice baths for in use portions of dressing until the until can be repaired.

Facility will call inspector when unit is functioning properly.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Salad dressings tomatoes and all salad items in the salad make table are between 48F and 51F. The items in the top were discarded in the garbage along with the pre portioned cups and packets of dressing, the larger containers of dressing were embargoed and the facility will provide information from the manufacturers concerning the shelf stable or perishable nature of the items. See embargo form for specific items. The unit was turned down and will not be used until it can maintain food at 41F or below. The violation was corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Roaches are observed emanating from the soiled linen bag. The facility has stuffed the bag full and packed it down. At least 4 roaches came out of the bag. All were eliminated. Orkin is the current pest control company and is present on site every other week. The facility should increase pest control efforts to weekly if acceptable per the chemicals being used. Facility should remove soiled linens nightly or put them into a container which keeps pests from finding food and harborage in the linens. Glue boards were removed from under the fryer next to hot line. At last routine inspection, there was a glue board at this location. Continue to use glue traps and other methods of riding the premises of pests.

A spot check on live roach activity will be conducted on 6/9/23. Until that time remove all harborage areas for insects including wall gaps from missing base cove, missing tiles by the walk in cooler, and any and all holes observed in the facility.

Also, there are broken tiles at the kitchen wall next to the walk in cooler. These base cove tiles if broken shall be replaced and if pulled away from the wall, sealed to the wall. Complete as much correction as possible before next inspection to help eliminate harborage for insects.

Area on the floor under the fryers next to the oven are heavily soiled with grease. Remove all food, water and shelter daily in order to get pests under control. End of the day cleaning is extremely important in the eradication of pests. Pests will not eat bait if there is other food to sustain them. Make concerted efforts to completely rid the facility of pests. Also the areas under the fryers themselves and other cleaning  areas discussed in the last routine inspection should be addressed regularly and maintained clean.

Observed employee drop single use gloves on the floor, pick them up and put them on his hands. The employee was stopped. He was coached concerning single use glove use and hand washing at time of inspection.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: Observed breadsticks in a tub of in-house created butter to be stored in the walk-in cooler with a date of 11/21. Only a few breadsticks remained - discarded upon request. Discussed the life of sauces created in-house and the movement of such in-house created sauces through the facility within seven days. Cease storing breadsticks IN house-made sauce longer than seven days.   

(A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple stacks of cups that were not properly air-dried after cleaning and sanitizing. Plastic cups had water/condensation remaining. Discussed proper cup air drying with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed the the drying racks of the dish machine area (shelving) to be extremely rusty and no longer corrosion-resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Replace these shelves.

Observed ponding ice water in the walk-in freezer. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas that are nonfood-contact surfaces to have soil residues and debris accumulation:
1. Fans of walk-in cooler observed to have dust. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20.
2. Walk-in freezer fans observed to have dust.
3. Spray nozzle observed to have grime and debris on and under nozzle (at dish machine area).
4. Shelving units throughout facility observed to have dust and grime (storage in front of pizza prep area, dish drying rack between walk-in cooler and freezer). This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20.
5. Reach-in cooler near pizza prep area has dusty fans within cooler and accumulation of food splash on the shelving units, as well as the base of the cooler.
6. Exterior of the reach-in coolers have food debris and grime on handles.
7. Hood baffles in need of deep cleaning - large accumulation of debris
8. Breading cart near stove and grill top observed to have large accumulation of grime, grease build-up, and food debris. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20. 

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure cleaning occurs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

(REPEAT) Observed mop to be hanging in a manner that does not allow to air and/or drip dry. Discussed with proper mop storage with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/14/20.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas to be no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Seal the particle board in the cupboards above ice/soda machine at both wait stations. Both cupboards contain stacked plastic cups. Seal with paint.
2. Re-caulk the kitchen hand sink. Caulk is coming away from the wall and moldy.
3. Caulk the dish machine to the wall. No caulk was present.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs are conducted before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas. 

Observed no light shield in the dish machine area. This light was directly above the drying racks. Discussed purchasing light shield with PIC.
